title: Complex Fractions

blocks.html: A complex fraction has fractions inside its numerator or denominator, like $\dfrac{1 - \frac{4}{x^2}}{1 + \frac{2}{x}}$. You can untangle it with tools from Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions and Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions.

Find the LCD of all the small fractions. Multiply the top and the bottom of the big fraction by it; every small denominator cancels. Then factor and simplify. (Another way: combine the top into one fraction, the bottom into one fraction, then divide.)

Multiplying the numerator and the denominator by the same nonzero expression is multiplying by 1, so the value doesn't change. Choosing the LCD makes every small fraction's denominator cancel at once, leaving a plain rational expression.

blocks.title: Clear with the LCD
steps: The small denominators are $x^2$ and $x$; the LCD is $x^2$.

blocks.title: A difference quotient
blocks.a: $-\frac{1}{x(x + 3)}$. (Expressions like this one appear in calculus.)

blocks.html: Multiplying only the small fractions by the LCD, or only the top of the big fraction. Whatever you multiply the numerator by, you must multiply the denominator by too. Check your answer by putting a number such as $x = 1$ into both the original and the simplified form.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: $f$ is the original complex fraction and $g$ is the simplified form $\frac{x - 2}{x}$. The two graphs lie on top of each other (the original has holes where $x = 0$ or $x = -2$).
